entries.title: Exodus 40:1
segments: The return of the seasons is well adapted to remind us of the goodness of God, and our obligations to him for his mercies.  And when, according to his will, we begin the year with devoutly acknowledging and adoring him, we may hope that whether we continue to its close in this world, or are removed to another, we shall still be happy in the service of God.

entries.title: Exodus 40:2
segments: The first day of the first month; they started from Egypt on the fifteenth day of the first month.  On the fiftieth day after, the law was given from mount Sinai; and Moses was eighty days in the mount.  A number of other things were done, and several delays occasioned, which must have occupied about six months, before the tabernacle was begun. As the first day of the first month would make a year from the time they left Egypt wanting fifteen days, they were probably employed not far from six months in preparing the tabernacle.

entries.title: Exodus 40:15
segments: Such is the nature of men, and such the ways in which they are most usefully impressed, that the setting apart of particular places for public worship, and of particular men to conduct it, is suited to promote their highest good.

entries.title: Exodus 40:17
segments: In the second year; after their departure from Egypt.

entries.title: Exodus 40:20
segments: The testimony; the tables containing the ten commandments, that solemn testimony of God with regard to the duty of men.

entries.title: Exodus 40:21
segments: The veil of the covering; that which covered or closed the entrance into the holy of holies, and thus prevented the ark from being seen, except by the high-priest once a year.

entries.title: Exodus 40:32
segments: The doing of all things as the Lord commands, is the sure way of promoting his glory, and of obtaining his blessing.  It is also the way to make our temporary sojourn on earth a preparation for an eternal dwelling with God in heaven.

entries.title: Exodus 40:33
segments:
Finished the work; the work of preparing the tabernacle according to the pattern which God showed, and the directions he gave to Moses in the mount. 
 
God's taking forty days to give directions about the tabernacle and its worship, and but six to create the world; and his occupying many chapters of the Bible to describe the former, and but one to describe the latter, should increase our conviction of the superiority of redemption to creation, and lead us to regard principally not things seen and temporal, but things unseen and eternal.

entries.title: Exodus 40:34
segments:
A cloud; that in which Jehovah dwelt. 
 
  The glory of the Lord; the resplendent brightness which manifested his presence.

entries.title: Exodus 40:36
segments: The cloud was taken up; and moved forward in the way that they should go.

entries.title: Exodus 40:38
segments: All the preparation that was made to provide a dwelling-place for God, and institute his worship among the Israelites, the glory which filled the tabernacle, his guidance of them by the pillar of cloud and fire in all their journey through the wilderness, and his introduction of them into Canaan, prefigured his dwelling in human nature and becoming the light of the world, that such as should follow him might be guided by his counsel and afterwards be received to glory.
